reasoning: Both work correctly and pass luau-lsp, selene and StyLua. A's failed disconnect check is a false alarm, because UnbindFromRenderStep tears down just as cleanly. A is slightly more defensive (a _destroyed guard, the check reason, a size inset), but B follows the project's conventions (const services, a Module table, PascalCase methods), which A breaks. With the functional quality about equal, B is the more merge-ready attempt.

criteria.note: BindToRenderStep runs _update every frame; it raycasts from the mouse excluding {character, self._part}, steps out by Normal*BlockSize/2 before PlacementRules.snap, hides by setting Transparency to 1 on a miss, and tints with BLOCKED_COLOR when PlacementRules.check fails against PlacedBlocks.
destroy() calls UnbindFromRenderStep(self._bindingName) and self._part:Destroy() behind a _destroyed guard. The failed 'disconnect' check is a false alarm, because unbinding is equivalent.

A Fields type with typeof(setmetatable({} :: Fields, GhostPreview)), all fields set in the constructor, and the part has CanCollide/CanQuery = false. It does not use the project's convention of naming the class table Module.
new(blockType: BlockType, options: Options?): GhostPreview; getPlacement returns (boolean, Vector3?, string?) and returns nil when hidden.
A named Options table with Transparency and RaycastDistance; DEFAULT_TRANSPARENCY and DEFAULT_RAYCAST_DISTANCE are named constants.
One class, nothing out of scope, and lint passes, but it breaks the repo conventions (local services instead of const, class table not named Module).
PreRender runs _Update; _RaycastFromMouse excludes the character and the part, steps half a block along the normal before snap, unparents the part on a miss, and tints red when check fails.
Destroy disconnects _Connection, sets it to nil, and destroys _Part; calling it twice is harmless.
The inline typeof(setmetatable({...}, Module)) type declares every field, all set in new; the part is non-colliding with CanQuery = false; it follows the Module convention.
Typed constructor and methods with () returns; GetPlacement returns (boolean, Vector3?).
An Options table with named DEFAULT_ constants, plus asserts on the values.
One class at the given path, nothing out of scope, and it passes every check, including the convention checks.
